newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Gecamines says rail stoppage report "exaggerated".
newsitem.headline: Gecamines says rail stoppage report "exaggerated".

text.p: A report that rail traffic, including cobalt and copper consignments, has ground to a halt in Zaire is exaggerated, Gecamines director of supplies and transport, Ntambo Luba, told Reuters by phone from Lubumbashi.
In Johannesburg, South African state-owned railway Spoornet said on Wednesday that Zaire's trains had stopped running after Laurent Kabila's rebels formed a new company to run the network.
Spoornet was a joint operator of Sizarail which resurrected Zaire's run-down railway network in eastern and southern Zaire and reopened supply routes to southern Africa.
"Traffic continues. There are some problems with the railway's partners and there are negotiations. But there is no total stoppage," said Luba from the company's headquarters.
It's not the first time there were problems between the railways partners, he added.
"I'm not aware of a major problem," he said.

Kabila's forces say they are less than 85 km from Kinshasa and have appealed to government troops to surrender to avoid a bloody takeover of the capital. Diplomatic sources say that the front line is more than 200 km from Kinshasa.
